input: This passage presents the results of a series of batch adsorption tests in which the adsorption of a dye from water onto a sample of zeolite 13X was measured under controlled laboratory conditions at a temperature of 298 K. The equilibrium data that were obtained from these tests were fitted to the Langmuir model, and the fitted Langmuir capacity of the adsorbent was found to be 195 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent, a value that was obtained at pH 6. In a separate practical test of the material, an adsorbent dose of 1.2 g L-1 was used, and under these conditions the removal achieved after a contact time of 120 min was 88% of the initial dye concentration, which had been set at 50 mg L-1 at the start of the experiment. It should be noted that the Langmuir fit is reported for pH 6 only, which is an important limitation of the work as presented, and the capacity of the zeolite at other pH values was not measured during this study, so no conclusions can be drawn about its performance across a wider pH range on the basis of these experiments alone.
target: Adsorption of a dye from water on zeolite 13X was measured in batch tests at 298 K. The Langmuir fit at pH 6 gives a capacity of 195 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent. Capacity here is the fitted monolayer capacity of the Langmuir model, the saturation value of the fitted isotherm rather than a loading measured at any single concentration. At an adsorbent dose of 1.2 g L-1, removal after 120 min was 88% of the initial dye concentration of 50 mg L-1. The two figures describe different quantities. The removal percentage belongs to one dose, one initial concentration and one contact time; it falls as the initial concentration rises toward the capacity limit, and it is not a property of the zeolite alone. The Langmuir fit is reported for pH 6 only. Capacity at other pH values was not measured, and dye adsorption on a zeolite surface is pH-sensitive through both the dye speciation and the surface charge, so the capacity figure carries no support outside that condition. Within that condition, the fit and the removal test agree in showing a high-capacity material at the tested concentration. The batch test also fixes the contact time at which removal is quoted, and removal continues to change while contact lasts; a shorter contact would report a lower removal for the same material and dose, and the comparison of adsorbents on removal percentage alone, without matched dose, concentration and contact time, ranks the experiments rather than the materials.
